answer: Anchor-delayed escrow admission prices identity in locked time. Each agent deposits 1,000 tokens into the epoch harbor; the epoch anchor hash draws its refund delay uniformly from 64-512 epochs at commit. A two-thirds witness quorum verifies the locked entry on admission; a convicted sybil forfeits its deposit, and one fraud whisper from any witness freezes maturing entries. Each identity locks a mean 288,000 token-epochs, so n identities pay linearly growing capital; resets fail because the delay is fixed by the anchor at commit and refunds go only to the original account.
